question: Can Delta unlimited wrapping requeue unchanged text and stop making progress when the next source grapheme cannot fit before the wrap marker, including with a valid one-column marker?

sources.name: dandavison/delta
sources.claim: wrap_line can requeue the complete source segment when the next grapheme does not fit the pre-marker width; unlimited mode has no line-count stop. The public marker validator separately counts graphemes rather than display columns.

sources.name: unicode-rs/unicode-width
sources.claim: Delta's exact target resolves unicode-width 0.1.14 for its direct width calculations; ordinary fullwidth CJK graphemes occupy two columns.

command: GitHub Actions: Fieldwork Delta wide wrap symbol probe

dependencies: exact dandavison/delta source fetched read-only at 95a0e224f55ccfdf3a7d1278fdea98a3edb9fbf4

distinguishing_outcomes.observation: With valid marker +, ASCII text at the same narrow width terminates, while text beginning with a two-column grapheme exceeds the watchdog.
distinguishing_outcomes.interpretation: The primary owner is a general no-progress split in wrap_line rather than only invalid marker validation.

distinguishing_outcomes.observation: The same valid-marker distinction reproduces through the built public delta command.
distinguishing_outcomes.interpretation: Promote the no-progress loop as a user-reachable current-head candidate.

distinguishing_outcomes.observation: A two-column one-grapheme marker is also accepted and triggers the same no-progress family.
distinguishing_outcomes.interpretation: Retain display-width validation as a second bug and defense layer, but keep the loop progress invariant primary.
